title: Interleaved-block KV quantization: stability and fidelity evaluation across workload slices
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Goal: Evaluate an interleaved-block KV-cache quantization strategy that reduces GPU memory footprint while keeping downstream quality and latency within SLOs for production inference workloads. This ticket defines experiments, success criteria, and runtime fallback logic exploration for mixed-precision KV representations (FP8/INT8/INT4) applied at block granularity and interleaved across slabs to reduce aliasing and fragmentation effects.

Background: Prior work explored per-shard and blockwise quantization (see dependency ENG-27103). Those probes highlighted that uniform low-bit quantization yields acceptable mean accuracy but brittle tail behavior for long-context workloads and for certain prompt cohorts. We propose an interleaved pattern that alternates precision across neighboring blocks (e.g., FP8/INT8/INT4/FP8) and a dynamic hot-key promotion policy to provide local high-fidelity paths for frequently-accessed keys. The hypothesis is that interleaving reduces correlated error accumulation across attention span and improves numerical stability for sequential KV accesses under continuous batching and KV reuse.

Experiment plan:
- Datasets/workloads: production anonymized traces (10M requests sampled across cohorts: chat-dialogue, summarization, code-assist, retrieval-augmented generation), and eval suites: MMLU-lite, summarization ROUGE set, LLM-perf long-context synthetic sequences (256/1024/4096 tokens).
- Hardware/config: dedicated test fleet on A100-80GB and H100-80GB nodes, single-GPU and 2-way model-parallel shards. Baseline: FP16 KV. Variants: FP8 uniform, INT8 uniform, INT4 uniform, and interleaved-block patterns (FP8/INT8 alternating, FP8/INT8/INT4 tri-pattern). Also test block size sweep: 64, 128, 256 vector elements.
- Metrics: memory savings (peak and steady), token generation latency P50/P90/P99 under continuous batching with realistic arrival distributions, downstream quality regressions (perplexity delta, ROUGE/EM delta, embedding cosine similarity), cohort-specific failure rates (>=5% confidence), and stability over long sessions (drift after 1k/4k tokens).
- Runtime controls and fallback: implement an on-request precision-tag carried in the router so that hot-paths can request FP8 fallback. Explore lightweight residue compensation where INT8 increments are adjusted by a tiny FP8 residual for hot keys. Instrument per-key access frequency and recency to evaluate hot-key promotion thresholds.
- Success criteria (pass/fail): memory reduction >= 40% vs FP16 without exceeding 4% relative degradation on primary QA metric for each cohort, and latency P99 increase <= 20ms. If cohort-specific regressions exceed thresholds, plan staged rollout with canary and automatic fallback to baseline for affected cohort.

Safety and trade-offs:
- Expected trade-offs include increased quantization noise for cold keys and edge-case modalities (low-SNR retrieval contexts). Interleaving may introduce non-deterministic behavior in rare sequences; tests will validate determinism across runs. Memory fragmentation observed in earlier experiments required allocator fixes; we will run updated allocator PRs before large sweeps.

Artifacts and links:
- Confluence design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/KV+Interleaved+Quant+Design
- GH prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6821 (prototype of interleaved encoder/decoder and residue compensator)
- Eval dashboards: https://dash.redwood.ai/kv-quant-eval/ENG-137256

Implementation notes:
- Code changes are limited to the KV storage layer and runtime quantization module; no API surface changes. We will add a compact on-disk format for persisted caches so that offline bake/test cycles reproduce the same bit patterns.
- Scheduler integration: ensure continuous-batching coalescer respects per-request precision flags to avoid cross-batch mixing that could violate SLOs.

Deliverables:
- Sweep results (memory/latency/quality) for FP8/INT8/INT4/uniform vs interleaved across block sizes and hardware types.
- Draft runtime fallback design and a canary rollout checklist.
- PRs for allocator fixes and prototype merged to internal experimental branch.

Success path: If interleaved-block FP8/INT8 provides >40% memory reduction with <2% quality regression and controllable latency, proceed to runtime-1.22 beta rollout on dedicated capacity limited to non-critical tenants. If not, evaluate hybrid policy: hot-cohort FP8 + cold INT8 with dynamic demotion.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Maya Patel: Kickoff meeting notes: scoped cohorts, agreed on datasets and baseline hardware. Decided to prioritize A100 runs first to speed iteration.

2026-02-25 - Ethan Liu: Implemented initial interleaved encoder and unit tests. Observed quantization mismatch with current KV serializer; opened PR #6821. Allocator edge-case causes minor fragmentation on repeated small writes.

2026-03-02 - Reliability Review (Jordan Kim): Noted P99 jitter in continuous-batching harness likely due to cross-batch precision mixing. Recommend adding precision tag propagation in coalescer. Marked for follow-up.

2026-03-05 - Ethan Liu: Ran 500k-request smoke sweep. Preliminary results: FP8 uniform reduces KV memory by ~48% vs FP16 with mean perplexity delta +1.8% on chat cohort; INT8 uniform reduces by ~54% but shows +4.9% perplexity delta on long-context summaries. Interleaved FP8/INT8 pattern reduced long-context drift relative to INT8 uniform (perplexity delta down from +4.9% to +2.1%), at cost of ~3% higher peak latency.

2026-03-07 - Design feedback (Priya Rao): Concern about user-visible tail regressions for code-assist. Suggested adding a short-lived hot-key window to promote recently-used keys to FP8; also recommended targeted eval on code-generation prompts.

2026-03-09 - Ethan Liu: Implemented hot-key promotion and residue compensator prototype. Re-ran A/B compare on code-assist cohort: error-rate reduced to baseline within noise. Preparing full sweep across 10M trace sample starting 2026-03-11.
2026-03-10 - PM review (Liam Chen): Confirmed prioritization for runtime-1.22 and asked for canary rollout plan and rollback criteria in next update.
